mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate (measured as the 1-month change in FEDFUNDS) indicates an active monetary tightening cycle that increases the discount rate for equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25 percentage points in the prior month, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that suppresses corporate earnings growth and increases equity risk premiums, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: The joint occurrence of a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS increase > 0.25pp) and a low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.0%) indicates a late-cycle monetary tightening phase that intensifies equity market stress, producing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting the trigger condition, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.0%), the tight labor market supports strong consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A rising labor market (measured as the 1-month change in PAYEMS > 50,000) indicates improving economic conditions that boost corporate earnings expectations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS rises by at least 50,000 in the prior month, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts exceed 1,400,000 annualized units (HOUST > 1400), it signals robust consumer spending and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST > 1400, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: The joint occurrence of high housing starts (HOUST > 1400) and strong industrial production (INDPRO > 102.0) indicates a synchronized economic expansion that boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods meeting the trigger condition, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a high GDP growth regime (GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.0%), the strong economic expansion supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 annualized growth > 2.0%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.
